pr_title: Add debounced submission on input in project search
pr_body:
Closes #9318 

Release Notes:

- Added debounced search submission on input in project search
pr_comments: We require contributors to sign our Contributor License Agreement, and we don't have @Tebro on file. You can sign our CLA at https://zed.dev/cla. Once you've signed, post a comment here that says '@cla-bot check'.
The cla-bot has been summoned, and re-checked this pull request!

Thanks for working on this!  I realized that we probably need to do some UI design work before being able to merge this feature.  Added some thoughts in [a comment on the issue](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/9318#issuecomment-2629531771).

If the `Option A` choices are made, then I think the need for `prevent_focus_results` will naturally go away - `enter` is always just a focus switch to the results, and focusing the results would cause the full set of search results to be loaded.  Please wait on implementation while we sort out what makes sense for the design.

To keep the merge queue cleaner, I will close this for now, given https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/9318#issuecomment-2642837268 and the related design discussions.

Thank you for the PR, will be interesting to see the updated version.

issue_context.title: enable type on search by default
issue_context.body: Summary: Other editors search as you type, whereas in Zed project search only happens after you press enter. VSCode: will search project when type every char Zed: have to press enter to search.
comments: Yes, I miss this interactive search feature in Emacs so much.
This is already a feature request, but I'm going to close it in favour of this one due to the number of upvotes it's already received.

Do we know if vscode implements any kind of string algorithm/optimization when a single character is typed or deleted (an obvious one that comes to mind is when adding a character to our search, we need only to filter through the results we already have rather than rerun on the entire codebase) and whether such optimizations would be significant enough to implement in zed as well?
For me personally the search is unusable without this feature. Both vscode and IDEs from jetbrains have it.
This would be a really nice enhancement.  I think there should be a setting for this which defaults to live search.  Rationale is that some might not want to spend laptop battery on live search.
I am giving this a try, have something working already.

On reviewing #24086 (thanks @Tebro!), I realized that adding this in a way that works well in all cases is not so straightforward - I probably shouldn't have marked this as "good first issue".  However, happy to help with adding this feature.

Specifically:

* Old results should stay visible until `N` lines of new results are loaded, to avoid them disappearing and reappearing.  `N` should be chosen so that it's typically at least the whole pane.

* Results on these live searches should be limited to `M` results for efficiency. For example, VS Code limits to 20000 results, but I think we might want a lower limit than this.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dad1f80-75e8-4c4d-9713-55755a94969f)

Some UI choices to be made (I've pinged @iamnbutler about this, lets wait on design to be sorted out before implementing)

* What limit for live searches (`M`) to choose?

    - Option A: Same as N - relatively low - so that these live searches are just an efficient preview.  I prefer this option.

    - Option B: Large number like VS Code's choice of 20000

* When is the full search performed?

    - Option A: When focus enters the search results, and `enter` just causes focus to switch to the results, same as the behavior on search within a file.  I prefer this option.

    - Option B: Display a message when results are incomplete saying that `enter` needs to be pressed to get the full results

If both option As are chosen then there is no need to have an upfront message that the results are incomplete.  The user might still see the end of the incomplete results if they scroll the results.  Two options there:

- Option A: Display a message at the end of the results indicating that they are incomplete, and explaining how to cause a full load.  I think I prefer this option.

- Option B: When scrolled, continue doing the rest of the search.  This seems a bit unconventional, and doesn't handle the case where the user has a large enough screen or tiny enough font that `N` results fits entirely on screen.
I like both of your A options from a user perspective. Seems like a good combination for performance and UX. I however am unlikely to be able to do that alone myself in any kind of short time frame.

review_comments: Is there a better way to handle this state?

Been trying to solve the issue of keeping the prevent_focus_results as struct field. I don't really like having it there but can't quite figure out how to make it proper. Any suggestions would be welcome.
